reviewer.independence_statement: The reviewer did not participate in Track A, Track B, Track C, pane5 arbitration, or item-level labeling. The review did not inspect item-level reviews, v60 actual outputs, or execution verdicts, and did not invoke a method, Judge, provider, or execution pipeline.

explicitly_excluded: item-level Track A, Track B, Track C, and arbitration files
v60 actual predicate or input output
method, Judge, provider, and hosted-LLM pipelines
input_scope.primary_source_policy: Claims were checked against original papers, the official OMG standard, publisher or author-institution records, author-hosted primary reports, or institutional-repository copies. Blogs and search-result snippets were not used as evidence.

decision_rule.claim_pass: PASS requires a primary or normative source, a DOI or stable formal URL, a verified locator, a directly verified short quotation, a bounded support reading, and an explicit non-support boundary.
decision_rule.claim_fail: FAIL applies when any required citation element is materially wrong or missing even if the underlying proposition can be repaired from the same source.
decision_rule.operationalization_rule: A disclosed project operationalization is not required to be stated verbatim by the motivating literature. It fails academic review only if it is falsely attributed to a source, presented as externally validated without evidence, or used without the semantic boundaries needed for the claim.
decision_rule.canonical_impact_rule: This review does not change canonical rows. An impact flag identifies whether future canonical item reasoning could depend on the academic or semantic correction.

claim_reviews.primary_source: Dwyer, Avrunin, and Corbett, Patterns in Property Specifications for Finite-State Verification, ICSE 1999
claim_reviews.verified_locator: IEEE Xplore document 841031, Abstract; no body page is claimed
verified_quotes: we proposed a pattern-based approach to the presentation, codification and reuse of property specifications for finite-state verification.
claim_reviews.support_assessment: The abstract directly supports reusable pattern-based codification of finite-state properties. Treating patterns as aids for structuring O is a bounded project use.
claim_reviews.non_support_boundary: The source does not establish completeness of the project's predicate registry, a universal precision order, or any item-level O/P equivalence.

claim_reviews.primary_source: Giannakopoulou et al., Formal Requirements Elicitation with FRET, CEUR-WS Vol. 2584, 2020
verified_quotes: A fretish requirement description is automatically parsed into six sequential fields
formalization verifier is a modular, extensible framework, which provides assurance that formulas generated by the formalizer capture the intended semantics.
claim_reviews.support_assessment: The paper names scope, condition, component, shall, timing, and response, explains temporal formula generation, and describes trace-based checking against independently generated expected values.
claim_reviews.non_support_boundary: FRET does not prove that a generated formula captures unstated author intent, covers every state-machine obligation, or validates this project's review workflow.
claim_reviews.recommended_fix: None. A second short quote about trace checking would improve the matrix but is not needed to rescue the verified locator.

claim_reviews.primary_source: Barr et al., The Oracle Problem in Software Testing: A Survey, IEEE TSE 41(5), 2015
verified_quotes: The ground truth oracle, G, is a total test oracle that always gives the 'right answer'.
The test oracle D is sound iff D(a) implies G(a).
claim_reviews.support_assessment: Definitions 2.7 and 2.8 give opposite implication directions, and the paper explicitly discusses partial test oracles. This supports directional adequacy reasoning.
claim_reviews.non_support_boundary: Barr does not define O, P, the four project labels, pane5, reviewer independence, or a guarantee that internal review recovers ground truth.

claim_reviews.primary_source: Beer et al., Efficient Detection of Vacuity in Temporal Model Checking, FMSD 18(2), 2001
claim_reviews.verified_locator: IBM Research publication record, Abstract; no paper page is claimed
verified_quotes: the formula is trivially valid because the pre-condition of the implication is not satisfiable
claim_reviews.support_assessment: The abstract directly supports antecedent failure as vacuous validity and motivates a non-vacuity check for implication-like true results.
claim_reviews.non_support_boundary: It does not validate repaired-artifact positive controls, contamination resistance, arbitrary non-temporal predicates, or a claim that one true control detects all vacuity.

claim_reviews.primary_source: Tretmans, Model Based Testing with Labelled Transition Systems, LNCS 4949, 2008
verified_quotes: If this model is valid, i.e., expresses precisely what the system under test should do, all these tests are also provably valid.
testing can only show the presence of errors, not their absence.
claim_reviews.support_assessment: The cited pages directly support model validity as a prerequisite for generated-test validity and the general incompleteness of testing.
claim_reviews.non_support_boundary: The chapter does not equate ioco with project O/P equivalence, certify FCSTM conversion, or prove completeness of the project's predicates or controls.

claim_reviews.primary_source: Object Management Group, OMG UML 2.5.1, formal/2017-12-05
verified_quotes: no specific approach is defined if there is no initial Pseudostate that exists within the Region.
It is the source for at most one Transition, which may have an associated effect Behavior, but not an associated trigger or guard.
claim_reviews.support_assessment: The normative standard supports both the structural constraints and the semantic variation point when a Region lacks an initial Pseudostate.
claim_reviews.non_support_boundary: UML does not identify the intended initial state for an issue or automatically govern a PlantUML/pyfcstm profile that declares different semantics.

claim_reviews.primary_source: Object Management Group, OMG UML 2.5.1, formal/2017-12-05
verified_quotes: Event occurrences are detected, dispatched, and processed by the StateMachine execution, one at a time.
When all orthogonal Regions have finished executing the Transition, the current Event occurrence is fully consumed
claim_reviews.support_assessment: The same clause defines stable wait points, one-at-a-time dispatch, trivial completion for a non-enabled non-deferred event, and full consumption after orthogonal transitions finish.
claim_reviews.non_support_boundary: UML leaves dispatch ordering undefined and does not equate offered, dispatched, discarded, processed, or fully consumed events with any project receipt field.

claim_reviews.primary_source: Abadi and Lamport, The Existence of Refinement Mappings, TCS 82(2), 1991; author-hosted SRC Research Report 29
claim_reviews.recorded_locator: Author-hosted SRC Research Report 29, Sections 1.1-1.2, printed pp. 1-3 (PDF pp. 7-9)
claim_reviews.verified_locator: Author-hosted SRC Research Report 29, Section 2.4, printed p. 11 (PDF p. 17)
verified_quotes: A specification S1 implements a specification S2 iff every externally visible behavior allowed by S1 is also allowed by S2.
claim_reviews.support_assessment: The proposition is supported, and Section 2.4 also gives the state and behavior conditions for a refinement mapping. The current matrix nevertheless fails its own exact-locator requirement because it points to the wrong sections and pages. Its stored short quote also says 'if every' where the source says 'iff every', so verified_original_text=true is not accurate.
claim_reviews.non_support_boundary: The source gives one-way behavioral inclusion for implementation. It does not make one-way implication equivalence, validate a local predicate mapping automatically, or erase observation, stuttering, timing, fairness, and semantic-profile differences.
claim_reviews.recommended_fix: Correct the locator in the claim matrix and protocol source table to Section 2.4, SRC report printed p. 11 (PDF p. 17), and correct the quotation from 'if every' to 'iff every'. Keep the journal DOI and author-hosted report URL distinct so the pagination source is unambiguous.
claim_reviews.canonical_impact_note: The citation record is wrong, but the source supports the project's bounded logical use. No item relation needs to change solely for this locator correction.

claim_reviews.primary_source: Harel and Naamad, The STATEMATE Semantics of Statecharts, ACM TOSEM 5(4), 1996
verified_quotes: A run consists of a series of detailed snapshots of the system's situation
each subsequent one is obtained from its predecessor by executing a step
claim_reviews.support_assessment: The source defines system behavior as runs responding to external stimuli and statuses linked by precisely defined steps.
claim_reviews.non_support_boundary: STATEMATE's next-step, event-lifetime, concurrency, and time semantics do not transfer automatically to UML, PlantUML, or pyfcstm.

claim_reviews.primary_source: Biere et al., Symbolic Model Checking without BDDs, TACAS 1999
claim_reviews.verified_locator: Section 1, printed p. 194; Section 6, printed p. 205
verified_quotes: the bound is the maximal length of a counterexample
we could not verify the liveness property completely. We only showed that there are no counterexamples of particular length k.
claim_reviews.support_assessment: The paper supports SAT-based counterexample search at explicit k and directly demonstrates the no-completeness-bound limitation.
claim_reviews.non_support_boundary: It does not justify an arbitrary project-derived k as an unbounded proof, certify an artifact-to-SAT encoding, or turn timeout/error into a Boolean result.

claim_reviews.primary_source: Clarke et al., Counterexample-Guided Abstraction Refinement, CAV 2000
verified_quotes: the abstract counterexample might not be valid. We say that such a counterexample is spurious.
does not correspond to an actual trace in the concrete model
claim_reviews.support_assessment: The source directly supports checking an abstract counterexample against concrete behavior before reporting it as valid.
claim_reviews.non_support_boundary: Concrete replay does not prove O/P equivalence, source attribution, parser/compiler fidelity, or the truth of an issue as worded.

cross_cutting_findings.title: The matrix's overall FAIL incorrectly treats disclosed project controls as requiring verbatim literature validation

evidence.locator: decision_rule.overall_pass; unsupported_protocol_claims ACADEMIC-GAP-001 and ACADEMIC-GAP-002; verdict.reason

cross_cutting_findings.assessment: The protocol explicitly and correctly calls three-track review, pane5, positive-control contamination checks, implication labels, and status taxonomy project-engineered controls. Literature can motivate their components without prescribing the workflow verbatim. The matrix therefore should not make external validation of this exact workflow a condition for academic source-coverage PASS. It may retain a separate limitation that control effectiveness has not been empirically validated.
cross_cutting_findings.recommended_fix: Separate named-claim provenance from project-method validation. After correcting actual citation gaps, set literature coverage according to the bounded named claims; retain three-track/pane5/positive-control as disclosed operationalization and avoid efficacy or ground-truth-recovery language unless a validation study is added.
cross_cutting_findings.canonical_impact_note: This affects the academic release verdict and claims of method validation, not item labels or item predicates.

cross_cutting_findings.title: The mandatory FinalState/no-outgoing/whole-machine termination distinction lacks a claim-to-source row

quotes: FinalState is a special kind of State signifying that the enclosing Region has completed.
Entering a terminate Pseudostate implies that the execution of the StateMachine is terminated immediately.
If the enclosing Region is directly contained in a StateMachine and all other Regions in that StateMachine also are completed, then it means that the entire StateMachine behavior is completed.

cross_cutting_findings.assessment: The distinction is substantively correct, but neither the initial-pseudostate claim nor the RTC claim covers completion and termination. A normal named leaf, a UML FinalState, a state with no outgoing transitions, region completion, a terminate Pseudostate, and backend terminated() must not be treated as interchangeable without proposition-specific source and mapping evidence.
cross_cutting_findings.recommended_fix: Add a bounded PG-UML-TERMINATION-2017 claim row with the locators and quotations above. State explicitly that OMG supports UML distinctions but does not prove that pyfcstm terminated() is equivalent to UML terminate or top-level FinalState completion; that equivalence needs a backend mapping certificate.
cross_cutting_findings.canonical_impact_note: Potentially affects future canonical rows whose O or P observes completion/termination. No item rows were inspected, so the affected set is unknown and must be identified by a separate non-horizontal audit.

cross_cutting_findings.title: No universal most-precise-predicate ordering is claimed
cross_cutting_findings.assessment: The protocol correctly defines exactness as project-level O <=> P under fixed semantics and explicitly rejects a universal S < G < R < V precision ranking. Candidate selection among equivalent properties is source- and assumption-sensitive rather than family-ranked.

cross_cutting_findings.title: O/P equivalence, vacuity, boundedness, and counterexample boundaries are properly separated
cross_cutting_findings.assessment: The false-proxy direction is logically correct: O implies P permits not-P to entail not-O. The protocol does not infer relation from a false run, does not treat a scenario witness as the universal property, requires source-backed bounds or completeness for exact bounded claims, and keeps replay/concrete-witness validity separate from O/P equivalence.

cross_cutting_findings.title: The capability audit is an internal source-level contract audit, not a literature-derived precision taxonomy
cross_cutting_findings.assessment: The audit consistently bounds each predicate by actual quantifier, scope, timing, observable, and approximation. Its FAIL/BOUNDARY labels concern frozen contracts and runtime capability, not an academic claim that one predicate family is universally more precise.
cross_cutting_findings.recommended_fix: None for academic provenance. Backend claims remain subject to a separate code/contract review, which was outside this review.

summary.overall_reason: Release should not proceed on the current academic record because the Abadi-Lamport locator is wrong and the mandatory UML completion/termination boundary has no claim row. Separately, the matrix must stop using absence of verbatim literature validation for disclosed project controls as the reason to fail literature coverage. The substantive O/P, vacuity, boundedness, counterexample, UML initial, and UML RTC boundaries otherwise pass.
